transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

Most hobs have built-in overheat protection that switches a zone or the whole hob off when the internal electronics get too hot, which is more likely on high settings after a few minutes. When it keeps happening, it usually means the hob isn't cooling itself properly, though exactly how it behaves depends on your hob type and brand, which we don't know yet. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the hob's cooling / ventilation. Now try switching a zone on. Is it working now, or still not?
it works again after a few mins, but cuts out again on high. whats causing it?

I can't say for certain yet, because it depends on what type of hob it is (gas, ceramic or induction) and exactly when and where it cuts out. Cutting out after a few minutes on high often points to a built-in safety feature switching it off, but the pattern of when it trips will help narrow down the cause. Next: Note when it trips - on switch-on, on a particular zone, or after a spill/clean. Let me know what you find.
its induction, samsung. mostly the big front zones when on high/boost. not after a spill or anything, just after a few mins of cooking

Check the hob's isolator switch (often a large switch on the wall or in a cupboard) is on, and look at the fuse box for a breaker that has switched off. If a breaker keeps tripping, don't keep resetting it. Was the isolator or a breaker off (and is it sorted), or were they all on?
its not tripping, it works fine again after a few mins. just cuts out on high. isolator/breaker wont be it
Next: Stop using it and isolate at the spur if there is any burning smell or scorching. Let me know what you find.
no burning smell or scorching, nothing like that. so what's causing it?

I can't say for certain yet, but cutting out only on high or boost and then working again after a few minutes often points to the hob's built-in overheat protection switching it off to cool down. Whether that's the cause, or something else like the boost function's normal time limit, depends on a few more details about exactly what it's doing. Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?
fan roars loudly just before it cuts out, and a little code flashes briefly but i didnt catch it. only started after new drawer unit was fitted under it a month ago
